newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy budget summit ends, no agreement reached.
newsitem.headline: Italy budget summit ends, no agreement reached.

text.p: The meeting between government backers and Prime Minister Romano Prodi to discuss the 1997 budget ended on Monday with centre-left parties unable to reach a deal on the package, Prodi's office said in a statement.
"We made some progress but a few points of disagreement remain," the statement, read out by a spokesman, said.
A further meeting between party leaders was expected before the government unveils the package at the end of the week, officials said.
"We will work to overcome (the problems) with the aim of guaranteeing Italy's entry into European monetary union as well as social fairness," the prime minister's statement said.
Newspapers said on Monday there was deadlock between Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and the hard left Communist Refoundation over pension and health spending.

"It is pointless trying to deny it, there are disagreements. We are carrying on talking even if I don't think we'll be able to strike a deal by the end of today," Gerardo Bianchi, leader of the centrist Popular Party, said after the meeting.
Green party leader Carlo Ripa di Meana said the various government parties would meet again before September 27.
The budget aims to cut 32.4 trillion lire off next year's deficit, but analysts are sceptical that this target can be met without action on pensions and health spending.
Refoundation, whose support is needed for the government to win a majority in the lower house of parliament, has said it will block any cuts on sensitive welfare spending.
Ciampi is eager to present as tough a budget as possible as he fights to prepare the economy for the launch of the planned single European currency in 1999.

At present Italy fails to meet any of the criteria established by the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to sign up for the Euro and a weak budget would put the country even further behind in its bid to meet the Maastricht terms. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
